bibl.title: Rapid and sustained symptom reduction following psilocybin treatment for anxiety and depression in patients with life-threatening cancer: a randomized

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: 29 patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression, given single-dose psilocybin or niacin, each with psychotherapy, in a crossover design
span.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial, 29 patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression were randomly assigned and received treatment with single-dose psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or niacin, both in conjunction with psychotherapy.

span.label: whether single moderate-dose psilocybin with psychotherapy reduces cancer-related anxiety and depression against an active placebo control
span.quote: The primary outcomes were anxiety and depression assessed between groups prior to the crossover at 7 weeks.

span.label: a double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial finding immediate, substantial and sustained improvement, with the mystical experience mediating the effect - independently of, and against a different comparator from, the companion trial in the same issue
span.quote: In conjunction with psychotherapy, single moderate-dose psilocybin produced rapid, robust and enduring anxiolytic and anti-depressant effects in patients with cancer-related psychological distress.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Prior to the crossover, psilocybin produced immediate, substantial, and sustained improvements in anxiety and depression and led to decreases in cancer-related demoralization and hopelessness, improved spiritual wellbeing, and increased quality of life.

span.label: clinically significant anxiety and depression in cancer patients, present in 30-40% in hospital settings and associated with worse medical outcomes
span.quote: Enduring clinically significant anxiety and/or depressive symptoms are common in patients with cancer, present in 30–40% of patients in hospital settings

span.label: double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial with niacin as the active control, both arms in conjunction with psychotherapy, primary outcomes assessed between groups before the crossover at 7 weeks
span.term: double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial with niacin as the active control, both arms in conjunction with psychotherapy, primary outcomes assessed between groups before the crossover at 7 weeks
span.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial, 29 patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression were randomly assigned and received treatment with single-dose psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or niacin, both in conjunction with psychotherapy.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE MYSTICAL EXPERIENCE IS THE ROUTE, AND THE PAPER SAYS IT IS ONE ROUTE AMONG SEVERAL: intensity of the subjective mystical experience significantly mediated clinical benefit at 6 weeks, and the authors add that it is likely one of several mediators rather than the mechanism
span.note: status: significantly mediated (e.g. suggestive of causality)
span.quote: The mystical experience is likely to be one of several mediators that transmit the effect of psilocybin to changes in anxiety and/or depression.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PSYCHO-SPIRITUAL MECHANISM OF ACTION - the mystical state of consciousness - offered as a candidate alongside the neurobiological account rather than instead of it
span.quote: This finding suggests a potential psycho-spiritual mechanism of action: the mystical state of consciousness.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: DIFFICULT EXPERIENCES ARE TREATED AS PART OF THE THERAPY, not as harm to be prevented: challenging encounters with cancer-related fearful imagery are read as the working-through, which is why transient anxiety is monitored and managed rather than counted as an adverse outcome
span.quote: Difficult experiences are not necessarily pathological and can be understood as part of the therapeutic process (e.g. working through cancer-related psychological or existential distress through challenging encounters or emotionally charged confrontations with cancer-related fearful imagery or symbolism)

span.label: the authors state four limits in one sentence: a relatively small sample, a non-representative population (62% women, 90% Caucasian), a crossover design that limited interpretation of benefit after the crossover, and a control with limited blinding
span.quote: This trial was limited by a relatively small sample size, a non-nationally representative cancer patient population (e.g. 62% women, 90% Caucasian), which decreases generalizability, a crossover design that limited the interpretation of clinical benefits after the crossover, and the use of a control with limited blinding.

span.label: the mystical experience is described as likely one of several mediators, so the mediation result does not identify the mechanism
span.quote: The mystical experience is likely to be one of several mediators that transmit the effect of psilocybin to changes in anxiety and/or depression.

span.label: which dimensions of the mystical experience matter, and what predicts or promotes them, is left as warranted future enquiry
span.quote: Further enquiry into how particular dimensions of the mystical experience relate to reductions in anxiety and/or depression in this population and others, and what factors best predict or promote mystical experiences, is warranted.

span.label: the authors say further empirical research is needed to establish safety and efficacy definitively - the claim is offered as promising rather than settled
span.quote: Further empirical research is needed definitively to establish its safety and efficacy.

span.label: the therapeutic proposal is conditional on appropriate psychotherapy accompanying the drug, so the intervention is a package rather than a pharmacotherapy
span.quote: Psilocybin, administered in conjunction with appropriate psychotherapy, could become a novel pharmacological-psychosocial treatment modality for cancer-related psychological and existential distress.

span.label: an ACTIVE placebo - niacin - rather than an inert one, so the control arm produces a noticeable somatic effect and participants cannot infer condition from feeling nothing
span.note: eliminates: participants inferring their arm from feeling nothing - niacin produces a noticeable somatic effect, though the authors still record the blinding as limited · outcome: partial
span.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial, 29 patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression were randomly assigned and received treatment with single-dose psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or niacin, both in conjunction with psychotherapy.

span.label: both arms received the same psychotherapy, so the psychological support is held constant and the comparison is of the drug rather than of the treatment package
span.note: eliminates: the psychotherapy rather than the drug as the active ingredient - both arms received the same psychological support · outcome: held
span.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial, 29 patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression were randomly assigned and received treatment with single-dose psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or niacin, both in conjunction with psychotherapy.

span.label: primary outcomes were assessed BETWEEN GROUPS BEFORE the crossover at 7 weeks, which preserves a clean parallel-group comparison inside a crossover design
span.note: eliminates: carryover from the first dose contaminating the efficacy estimate - the primary comparison is between groups BEFORE the crossover · outcome: held
span.quote: The primary outcomes were anxiety and depression assessed between groups prior to the crossover at 7 weeks.

span.label: the trial was pre-registered - ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00957359
span.note: eliminates: outcome-switching and selective reporting - the trial was registered before it ran · outcome: held
span.quote: Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT00957359

span.label: safety is set against an external base rate: approximately 2000 doses of psilocybin administered in controlled settings since the early 1990s with no serious medical or psychiatric adverse events, no prolonged psychosis and no HPPD
span.note: eliminates: this trial's clean safety record being a small-sample artefact - it is set against roughly 2000 controlled doses since the early 1990s with no serious adverse events · outcome: held
span.quote: Since the early 1990s, approximately 2000 doses of psilocybin (ranging from low to high doses) have been safely administered to humans in the United States and Europe, in carefully controlled scientific settings, with no reports of any medical or psychiatric serious AEs, including no reported cases of prolonged psychosis or HPPD

span.label: psilocybin
span.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial, 29 patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression were randomly assigned and received treatment with single-dose psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or niacin, both in conjunction with psychotherapy.

span.label: niacin
span.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial, 29 patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression were randomly assigned and received treatment with single-dose psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or niacin, both in conjunction with psychotherapy.

span.label: crossover
span.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial, 29 patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression were randomly assigned and received treatment with single-dose psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or niacin, both in conjunction with psychotherapy.

span.label: psychotherapy
span.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial, 29 patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression were randomly assigned and received treatment with single-dose psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or niacin, both in conjunction with psychotherapy.

span.label: mystical experience
span.quote: The psilocybin-induced mystical experience mediated the therapeutic effect of psilocybin on anxiety and depression.

span.label: demoralization
span.quote: Prior to the crossover, psilocybin produced immediate, substantial, and sustained improvements in anxiety and depression and led to decreases in cancer-related demoralization and hopelessness, improved spiritual wellbeing, and increased quality of life.

span.label: hopelessness
span.quote: Prior to the crossover, psilocybin produced immediate, substantial, and sustained improvements in anxiety and depression and led to decreases in cancer-related demoralization and hopelessness, improved spiritual wellbeing, and increased quality of life.

span.label: spiritual wellbeing
span.quote: Prior to the crossover, psilocybin produced immediate, substantial, and sustained improvements in anxiety and depression and led to decreases in cancer-related demoralization and hopelessness, improved spiritual wellbeing, and increased quality of life.

span.label: existential distress
span.quote: At the 6.5-month follow-up, psilocybin was associated with enduring anxiolytic and anti-depressant effects (approximately 60–80% of participants continued with clinically significant reductions in depression or anxiety), sustained benefits in existential distress and quality of life, as well as improved attitudes towards death.

span.label: quality of life
span.quote: Prior to the crossover, psilocybin produced immediate, substantial, and sustained improvements in anxiety and depression and led to decreases in cancer-related demoralization and hopelessness, improved spiritual wellbeing, and increased quality of life.

span.label: HPPD
span.quote: Since the early 1990s, approximately 2000 doses of psilocybin (ranging from low to high doses) have been safely administered to humans in the United States and Europe, in carefully controlled scientific settings, with no reports of any medical or psychiatric serious AEs, including no reported cases of prolonged psychosis or HPPD

span.label: placebo - IN THIS TRIAL NIACIN, AN ACTIVE PLACEBO CHOSEN TO PRODUCE A NOTICEABLE SOMATIC EFFECT, not an inert capsule. The companion trial in the same issue used a very low dose of psilocybin instead. Two teams reached the same result through two different solutions to the same problem - that an inert placebo is unblindable against a psychedelic
span.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial, 29 patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression were randomly assigned and received treatment with single-dose psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or niacin, both in conjunction with psychotherapy.

span.label: mystical experience - A MEASURED MEDIATOR AND EXPLICITLY NOT THE ONLY ONE: the authors say it is `likely to be one of several mediators`, which is a weaker and more careful claim than the abstract's `mediated the therapeutic effect`
span.quote: The mystical experience is likely to be one of several mediators that transmit the effect of psilocybin to changes in anxiety and/or depression.

span.label: difficult experience - NOT AN ADVERSE EVENT IN THIS FRAMEWORK. Transient anxiety or paranoia is to be monitored and managed, and is read as part of the therapeutic process rather than as harm, which changes what the safety numbers of a psychedelic trial mean
span.quote: Difficult experiences are not necessarily pathological and can be understood as part of the therapeutic process (e.g. working through cancer-related psychological or existential distress through challenging encounters or emotionally charged confrontations with cancer-related fearful imagery or symbolism)

span.label: replicates → prior trials of psilocybin in NORMAL VOLUNTEERS (Griffiths et al. 2006, 2008, 2011) and in patients with terminal cancer (Grob et al. 2011), whose mystical-type effects this trial reproduces
span.note: differs in: the population - the earlier mystical-experience results are in healthy volunteers, and this trial finds them in patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression
span.quote: Compared to the control, psilocybin produced mystical-type experiences, consistent with prior trials of psilocybin administration in normal volunteers ( Griffiths et al., 2006, 2008, 2011) and patients with terminal cancer ( Grob et al., 2011) ( Figure 7 (top)).

span.label: confirms → the adverse-event profile reported in earlier psilocybin trials in normal volunteers and in terminal cancer patients, which this trial's transient and tolerable events match
span.quote: psychiatric AEs (transient anxiety, transient near-psychotic symptoms) attributable to psilocybin are all known AEs of psilocybin, were transient, tolerable, and consistent with prior trials of psilocybin administration in normal volunteers ( Griffiths et al., 2006, 2008, 2011), and patients with terminal cancer ( Grob et al., 2011).

span.label: confirms → the cardiovascular safety, time course and magnitude observed in previous psilocybin studies in healthy volunteers and advanced cancer patients
span.quote: The medical safety, time course, and magnitude of effects on these cardiovascular measures were consistent with those observed in previous studies of psilocybin in healthy volunteers ( Griffiths et al., 2006, 2011) and patients with advanced cancer ( Grob et al., 2011).

span.label: confirms → open-label LSD-assisted psychotherapy trials for terminal cancer distress, in which the mystical experience was described as integral to the therapeutic effect
span.quote: This result matches with descriptive historical data from open-label LSD-assisted psychotherapy trials for psycho-spiritual distress associated with terminal cancer, in which the mystical experience was reported as being an integral part of the therapeutic effect

span.label: confirms → open-label psilocybin trials for tobacco addiction and alcoholism, which report the same correlation between mystical experience and outcome
span.quote: It is further corroborated by recent open-label trials using psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy to treat tobacco addiction ( Garcia-Romeu et al., 2014; Johnson et al., 2014) and alcoholism ( Bogenschutz et al., 2015) showing significant correlations between the mystical experience and improved clinical outcomes.

span.label: critiques → existing pharmacotherapeutic and psychosocial treatment for cancer-related anxiety and depression, whose efficacy is called mixed and limited and for which no FDA-approved pharmacotherapy exists
span.quote: There are no US Food and Drug Administration approved pharmacotherapies for cancer-related psychological distress, the onset of clinical improvement with anti-depressants is delayed, relapse rates are high, and significant side effects compromise treatment adherence

span.label: psilocybin —causes→ existential distress
span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: At the 6.5-month follow-up, psilocybin was associated with enduring anxiolytic and anti-depressant effects (approximately 60–80% of participants continued with clinically significant reductions in depression or anxiety), sustained benefits in existential distress and quality of life, as well as improved attitudes towards death.

span.label: psilocybin —causes→ quality of life
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: Prior to the crossover, psilocybin produced immediate, substantial, and sustained improvements in anxiety and depression and led to decreases in cancer-related demoralization and hopelessness, improved spiritual wellbeing, and increased quality of life.

span.label: mystical experience —causes→ psilocybin
span.quote: The psilocybin-induced mystical experience mediated the therapeutic effect of psilocybin on anxiety and depression.

span.label: niacin —operationalised-as→ psychotherapy
span.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial, 29 patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression were randomly assigned and received treatment with single-dose psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or niacin, both in conjunction with psychotherapy.

span.label: before the crossover, psilocybin produced immediate, substantial and sustained improvement in anxiety and depression, with decreases in demoralization and hopelessness and increases in spiritual wellbeing and quality of life
span.quote: Prior to the crossover, psilocybin produced immediate, substantial, and sustained improvements in anxiety and depression and led to decreases in cancer-related demoralization and hopelessness, improved spiritual wellbeing, and increased quality of life.

span.label: at 6.5-month follow-up roughly 60-80% of participants still showed clinically significant reductions in depression or anxiety, with sustained benefit in existential distress and improved attitudes towards death
span.quote: At the 6.5-month follow-up, psilocybin was associated with enduring anxiolytic and anti-depressant effects (approximately 60–80% of participants continued with clinically significant reductions in depression or anxiety), sustained benefits in existential distress and quality of life, as well as improved attitudes towards death.

span.label: the psilocybin-induced mystical experience mediated the effect on anxiety and depression
span.quote: The psilocybin-induced mystical experience mediated the therapeutic effect of psilocybin on anxiety and depression.

span.label: no serious medical or psychiatric adverse events in the trial were attributed to psilocybin
span.quote: There were no serious AEs, either medical or psychiatric, in the trial that were attributed to psilocybin.

span.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial, 29 patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression were randomly assigned and received treatment with single-dose psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or niacin, both in conjunction with psychotherapy.

span.quote: Since the early 1990s, approximately 2000 doses of psilocybin (ranging from low to high doses) have been safely administered to humans in the United States and Europe, in carefully controlled scientific settings, with no reports of any medical or psychiatric serious AEs, including no reported cases of prolonged psychosis or HPPD

span.term: drug condition, single-dose psilocybin 0.3 mg/kg against niacin
span.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial, 29 patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression were randomly assigned and received treatment with single-dose psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or niacin, both in conjunction with psychotherapy.

span.label: intensity of the subjective mystical experience, tested as a mediator
span.term: intensity of the subjective mystical experience, tested as a mediator
span.quote: Moderate-dose psilocybin occasioned mystical-type experiences in the cohort of cancer patients studied, and the intensity of the subjective mystical experience significantly mediated (e.g. suggestive of causality) clinical benefit (e.g. reduction in anxiety and depression symptoms) in the medium term (e.g. 6 weeks post-dose 1).

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1177/0269881116675512.
